descriptions.job-1qwbfom:
About us

BVNK is the stablecoin-powered financial stack for enterprises. We're now part of Mastercard, and together we're building a network for every form of money – one that delivers more reach, more capability and more choice.

We enable businesses to build financial products, unlock new markets, and move money in seconds across 130+ countries, with 40+ licenses for fiat and digital assets globally. Processing billions annually, we empower enterprises worldwide to send, receive, convert, and settle stablecoins and fiat seamlessly through a single integration.

Our mission is to accelerate global money movement, and we're assembling a world-class team to make it happen.

Trusted by industry leaders like Corpay, Worldpay, Deel, and Flywire, we deliver the infrastructure that makes new forms of money usable within the financial systems customers already rely on today.

By combining Mastercard's global payment reach and trusted networks with BVNK's stablecoin infrastructure, we're building the trusted operating layer for the evolution of money movement, helping customers participate in emerging digital networks without having to rebuild their businesses around every new innovation.

We're a diverse team spread across EMEA, North America, and APAC, with a shared belief that stablecoins are the new infrastructure layer for financial services, and that BVNK is at the forefront of this shift.

We're incredibly honored to have been recognized by:

  • CNBC World's Top Fintech Companies (2026)
  • FXC Intelligence Top 100 Cross-border Payment Companies (2026)
  • Newsweek's The Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces (three years running, most recently 2025)
  • LinkedIn as one of the Top 20 Startups in the UK (2025)

About this role in the team:

We are looking for an experienced Managing Director - UK to lead BVNK’s UK regulated entity, an FCA-authorised electronic money institution, as it seeks FCA authorisation for cryptoasset services.

This is a critical leadership appointment, responsible for establishing and maintaining a strong UK-regulated business while supporting BVNK's broader ambition to transform global money movement through stablecoin and payment infrastructure.

As Managing Director - UK, you will have overall executive accountability for the UK entity's strategy, financial performance, regulatory compliance and governance. You will work closely with the Board, UK senior management and wider BVNK and Mastercard leadership to ensure the business operates effectively within its regulatory permissions and maintains appropriate local decision-making authority.

The position will carry Senior Management Functions SMF1 and SMF3, subject to FCA approval, and will play a central role in demonstrating effective UK mind and management to the regulator.

You will be expected to lead engagement with the FCA throughout the authorisation process and establish a sustainable, commercially successful and well-controlled regulated business.

Key Areas of Responsibilities:

  • Provide overall executive leadership of BVNK UK, with accountability for its strategy, commercial performance, governance and regulatory obligations.
  • Lead the UK entity through the FCA authorisation process, acting as a key point of contact for regulatory engagement, assessments and interviews.
  • Establish and maintain effective UK-based governance, ensuring appropriate decision-making authority, management oversight and accountability within the regulated entity.
  • Hold the FCA approvals required for the role, including as a Senior Manager (SMF1 and SMF3) and as a director or manager of the electronic money institution, fulfilling the associated regulatory obligations and maintaining compliance with the Senior Managers and Certification Regime.
  • Take responsibility for the firm's Senior Managers Regime obligations, Certification Regime arrangements and Conduct Rules training.
  • Oversee the firm's financial resources and prudential compliance across its e-money and cryptoasset activities, including capital and liquidity adequacy, fixed overhead requirements, financial forecasting, stress testing and wind-down planning.
  • Own the commercial strategy and financial performance of the UK entity, leading UK commercial teams, balancing sustainable growth with regulatory requirements and effective risk management.
  • Ensure appropriate governance and oversight of the firm's cryptoasset, e-money and payment services, working closely with the COO and relevant control functions.
  • Oversee local marketing activities and compliance with applicable financial promotions requirements and ensure appropriate controls are maintained.
  • Lead the implementation and ongoing oversight of Consumer Duty requirements where applicable to the firm's regulated activities.
  • Work closely with Compliance, Risk, Finance and Operations to establish an effective three lines of defence model, with clear responsibilities, appropriate independence and robust escalation arrangements.
  • Maintain effective oversight of material risks, ensuring the Board receives appropriate management information and that significant regulatory or operational issues are escalated promptly.
  • Establish effective working relationships with Mastercard and BVNK group leadership, ensuring appropriate oversight of intra-group dependencies while preserving the UK entity's regulatory accountability.
  • Chair or attend relevant local and group-level committees and/or forums, providing effective challenge and ensuring the local entity is properly represented.
  • Build and lead a high-performing UK senior management team, promoting a culture of accountability, integrity, customer protection and regulatory compliance.
  • Represent BVNK UK with regulators, strategic partners and other key stakeholders.

What we need from you:

  • Significant senior executive leadership experience within a UK-regulated financial services business, ideally having previously held an FCA-approved SMF1 or SMF3 position.
  • Demonstrable experience running or holding substantial executive accountability within a regulated entity, including engagement with the FCA and responsibility for regulatory governance.
  • Strong knowledge of the UK financial services regulatory environment, including the Senior Managers and Certification Regime, governance requirements and individual accountability.
  • Experience within payments, electronic money, cryptoassets, digital assets or a closely related financial services sector.
  • A strong understanding of the regulatory and operational risks associated with cryptoasset custody and trading activities.
  • Sound knowledge of prudential requirements, including capital and liquidity adequacy, fixed overhead requirements, financial resource planning, stress testing and wind-down planning.
  • Understanding of Consumer Duty requirements, financial promotions and the associated governance and oversight expectations.
  • Experience developing and executing commercial strategies while maintaining effective regulatory controls and financial discipline.
  • Demonstrable ability to lead cross-functional senior management teams and oversee complex operational, financial and regulatory activities.
  • Strong understanding of risk management frameworks, governance structures and the three lines of defence model.
  • Experience working within a wider group structure, with the ability to balance group strategy and shared services with local regulatory accountability.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including the confidence and credibility to engage directly with regulators, Board members and senior executives.
  • Ability to demonstrate the fitness and propriety standards required for FCA Senior Manager approval, including honesty, integrity, competence, capability and financial soundness.
  • Willingness and ability to be based in the UK on a full-time basis, providing effective local leadership and regulatory oversight.

What you can expect from us:

  • Fair and competitive salary at every stage of your growth
  • Flexible working hours, with hybrid working at its heart
  • A culture built on passionate, growth-minded people
  • A flexible approach to holiday
  • Opportunities to travel to our offices around the world
  • An open and creative environment where you can help us define the future of BVNK, its culture, and its opportunity sets

At BVNK, we are focused on building a diverse and inclusive team. While you may not meet all of our requirements, we’d encourage you to apply if you meet the majority of our expectations. You may be a great fit for this role or another role in our team.

descriptions.job-0kwezmu:
About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market. In the US, Polymarket operates a CFTC-regulated exchange (DCM) and clearinghouse (DCO), and we're building the infrastructure to bring event contracts to a much wider set of customers and partners. Engineering here is small, senior, and close to the business: the systems you build move real money under real regulatory obligations.

About the role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the teams that move, clear, and protect customer funds on Polymarket US. You'll own our clearing, payments, and risk systems, and you'll lead engineering for our Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) build, one of the most important initiatives in the company. This role needs a manager who has built these systems before and understands the regulatory model behind them, not one who will learn it on the job.

What you'll do

  • Lead engineering for the FCM program end to end: customer onboarding and account structure, customer fund segregation, margin and collateral, and the integration between the FCM and our clearinghouse.
  • Own the clearing engine and the post-trade path: settlement, position and balance management, reconciliation, and the ledger that sits underneath all of it.
  • Own payments: deposits and withdrawals across bank, card, and wallet rails, fraud and risk checks at authorization, and the processor and banking partners behind them.
  • Build risk controls that run in real time: pre-trade and pre-funding checks, exposure limits, and the monitoring that tells us when something is wrong before a customer or regulator does.
  • Work daily with Clearing Operations, Treasury, Compliance, Legal, and the DCO/FCM business leads to turn regulatory and operational requirements into systems that hold up under audit.
  • Hire, grow, and manage a team of senior engineers. Set the technical bar, run on-call, and stay close enough to the code to make good design calls.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years in software engineering and 2+ years managing engineers, with a track record of shipping financial systems in production.
  • Direct subject-matter experience with at least two of: FCM operations, clearing and settlement, payments infrastructure. Ideally you've built these at an FCM, futures or crypto derivatives exchange, broker-dealer, or payments company.
  • Working knowledge of the CFTC framework for customer funds: segregation, margining, daily reconciliation and reporting, and what regulators expect from the systems that produce them.
  • Strong instincts for money-movement correctness: double-entry ledgers, idempotency, reconciliation, and failure handling across external partners.
  • Comfort leading a 0-to-1 build at startup speed while keeping the controls a regulated business needs.
  • Clear written communication with both engineers and non-technical partners in operations, finance, and compliance.

•(Plus) Experience standing up a new FCM, DCO, or derivatives clearing member, or taking one through a regulatory review.

•(Plus) Background with margin methodologies (for example SPAN-style models) or collateral management.

•(Plus) Experience with stablecoin or on-chain settlement rails alongside traditional banking rails.

•(Plus) Hands-on experience in Go or another systems language used for high-throughput services.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Health, vision, and dental coverage

  • 401(k) match

  • Full hardware setup: new MacBook Pro, large display, and accessories


Pay Transparency

Base salary range: $350,000 to $500,000 annually, plus equity and benefits.

This range reflects a good-faith estimate for this position. Experience levels vary widely within a title here, so please reach out even if your expectations fall outside it. We're always happy to chat.
descriptions.job-16p85ly:
Logos is a movement supporting the development of the decentralised web. Logos technologies lay the foundations for a freer internet upon which communities can evolve into network states. Each protocol in the Logos stack seeks to empower its users while upholding civil liberties and fundamental freedoms.

About Logos (λ)

Logos (λ) is a movement of technologists, creatives, strategists, and activists working together to build a sovereign, people-owned technology stack that revitalises civil society and protects digital liberties at scale.

This position is within the IFT Technical Services (IFT-TS) Distributed Systems Testing (DST) Team, a team that primarily supports Logos, while also contributing to other IFT projects.

The role

We are seeking an experienced Distributed Systems Evaluation Engineer to join the Institute of Free Technology - Technical Services, on the Distributed Systems Testing (IFT-TS DST) team. This role focuses on rigorously assessing the performance and reliability of IFT projects at scale, where Logos (λ) is one of them.
Logos (λ) technology stack is composed of 3 main components:

  • Logos (λ) Blockchain: Advanced privacy for a new era of decentralised applications and social institutions.
  • Logos (λ) Messaging: Private peer‑to‑peer communication that resists surveillance and censorship.
  • Logos (λ) Storage: Secure decentralised storage enabling fully decentralised apps and file sharing.

We are looking for a talented and enthusiastic DevOps Engineer to join our Distributed Systems Testing (DST) team.
You’ll be responsible for designing and executing comprehensive evaluation strategies, leveraging both large-scale lab deployments and protocol behavior modeling scripts. Your expertise will be crucial in analyzing these complex distributed systems, automating intricate test scenarios, and providing in-depth insights into system behaviors.
Working closely with cross-functional teams, you’ll troubleshoot complex issues and translate technical data into actionable recommendations. Proficiency in containerization, cloud technologies, and distributed systems principles is essential.

Key responsibilities

  • Design, configure, and optimize Kubernetes clusters to support large-scale experiments and benchmarks of P2P technologies.
  • Continuously improve cluster scalability and resource utilization, enabling increasingly complex deployments and experiments.
  • Set up, maintain, and optimize supporting infrastructure such as monitoring, logging, and observability stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, etc.).
  • Collaborate with DST researchers and engineers to streamline experimentation workflows and make analysis easier and more reproducible.
  • Automate infrastructure and deployment workflows to increase reliability and reduce overhead.
  • Troubleshoot, profile, and tune distributed workloads to ensure accurate and performant benchmarking.
  • Identify, reproduce, and debug complex issues in distributed systems, working closely with Logos development teams.

You ideally will have

  • Strong experience with Kubernetes and container orchestration in production or research environments.
  • Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure, Linux systems, and networking (especially relevant to distributed/P2P systems).
  • Familiarity with monitoring and logging tools (Grafana, Prometheus, VictoriaLogs, etc.).
  • Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible, Helm, etc.).
  • Proficiency in at least one scripting/programming language (ideally Python).
  • Interest in or experience with distributed systems, P2P networks, or blockchain technologies.
  • Experience with networks and systems programming.
  • Excellent written and conversational communication skills.
  • Alignment with our core values and principles.

Bonus points

  • Hands-on experience with libp2p or projects in the Logos collective.
  • Background in performance benchmarking, scalability testing, or systems research.
  • Contributions to open source projects.
  • Experience working for an open-source organization.

Interview Process

  • Interview with our POps team
  • Interview with team member from the IFT-TS DST team
  • Pair programming & discussion of results
  • Interview with IFT-TS team lead
descriptions.job-0z7kfdy:
Circle (NYSE: CRCL) is one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies, building the foundation of a more open, global economy through digital assets, payment applications, and programmable blockchain infrastructure. Circle’s platform includes the world’s largest regulated stablecoin network anchored by USDC, Circle Payments Network for global money movement, and Arc, an enterprise-grade blockchain designed to become the Economic OS for the internet. Enterprises, financial institutions, and developers use Circle to power trusted, internet-scale financial innovation. Learn more at circle.com.

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. We have built a flexible work environment where new ideas are encouraged and everyone is a stakeholder.

What you’ll be responsible for:

Circle is looking for an experienced transactional attorney to join the Transactions team within Circle’s Legal department. This role will focus primarily on two connected areas: Corporate Development and Ventures, including mergers and acquisitions, strategic transactions, and venture investments; and Financial Partnerships, including agreements with banks and other financial institutions that support Circle’s reserve, treasury, and payments operations. As needs arise, the role may also support select commercial transactions involving Circle’s products and services for banks and other financial institutions.

Under the direction of the Deputy Assistant General Counsel, Transactions, you will work as a senior individual contributor and trusted advisor to Circle’s Corporate Development and Ventures, Treasury, and Financial Partnerships teams, and will partner with Business Development, Product, and other teams on select matters as needed. You will independently lead transactions from inception through negotiation, signing, closing, and, where relevant, implementation or integration. This role requires rigorous legal execution, practical business judgment, and a solutions-oriented approach in a fast-moving digital asset and payments environment.

What you'll work on:

  • Supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, asset purchases, and other strategic transactions, including structuring, conducting due diligence, drafting definitive agreements, and coordinating signing, closing, and integration matters.
  • Advising on joint ventures, minority and venture investments, strategic partnerships with an equity component, and other non-ordinary-course transactions, including term sheets, investment agreements, side letters, and ancillary agreements.
  • Structuring, drafting, and negotiating agreements with banks and financial institutions supporting Circle’s reserve, treasury, and payments operations, including deposit, custody and safeguarding, account control, and cash management arrangements.
  • Serving as a trusted partner to Circle’s Corporate Development and Ventures, Treasury, and Financial Partnerships teams, leading transactions that involve Legal, Regulatory, Risk, Compliance, Tax, Corporate Governance, Product, and other stakeholders, and coordinating with outside counsel where appropriate.
  • As needs arise, supporting select commercial transactions in which Circle provides products, services, or technology to banks and other financial institutions, partnering with Business Development, Product, and Legal subject matter experts to translate business objectives into practical contractual terms.
  • Developing and expanding transaction templates, playbooks, diligence tools, processes, and metrics that increase speed, consistency, and effectiveness across recurring transaction types.
  • Helping design and lead the adoption of AI-enabled workflows across the Transactions team, rethinking how transactional legal work is structured and delivered, and using AI and other technology to improve diligence, contract review, issues lists, drafting, deal tracking, and other recurring workflows. Experimenting with new approaches, developing scalable processes and playbooks, and taking responsibility for reviewing and validating AI-assisted work product for accuracy, confidentiality, privilege, and risk.

How this role uses AI:

This role will use AI as a core part of day-to-day transactional work and will help shape how the Transactions team operates in an AI-enabled environment. We are looking for someone who is interested not only in using new tools, but also in rethinking how legal work gets done—identifying which parts of the transactional process can be redesigned, streamlined, or automated while preserving high standards of legal judgment and client service.

In practice, that means using AI tools to accelerate due diligence, review counterparty drafts against Circle’s playbooks and prior positions, prepare first drafts of issues lists, term sheets, and ancillary documents, and keep deal trackers and precedent current. The role will also identify recurring workflows where AI can improve speed and consistency, design and test new approaches, build and refine prompts, templates, and playbooks for AI-enabled work, and help other attorneys, interns, and business partners adopt effective practices.


The attorney remains fully responsible for the work. They will review and validate AI-assisted outputs for accuracy and legal judgment, protect privilege, confidentiality, and material non-public information, and follow Circle’s AI, security, and data policies. We are looking for someone who is curious, experimental, and excited to help rethink how a modern transactions practice operates, while using AI to augment—not replace—independent legal judgment.


What you’ll bring to Circle:

Core Requirements:

  • J.D. or foreign equivalent and active membership in good standing of at least one U.S. State Bar.
  • 7+ years of transactional legal experience at a leading law firm, an in-house legal department, or a combination of both.
  • Substantial experience with M&A and other corporate transactions, financial services transactions, or both, including structuring transactions, drafting first-turn agreements, leading negotiations and diligence, and independently driving complex matters through signing and closing.
  • Strong working knowledge of corporate and commercial law, sound business judgment, and the ability to coordinate legal, regulatory, tax, accounting, securities, and operational considerations while balancing legal risk, commercial objectives, and Circle’s strategic goals.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong ownership and organization, and the ability to manage multiple matters simultaneously in a fast-moving environment that is prone to rapid change.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with and practical use of generative AI in legal or other professional workflows, with sound judgment about when and how to use AI, validate outputs, and protect privileged, confidential, and material non-public information in a public company environment.
  • Passion for Circle’s mission and values, financial technology, and the potential of stablecoins, digital assets, and blockchain technology.


Preferred Requirements:

  • Experience with banking, deposit, custody, safeguarding, treasury, or other financial services agreements and/or seller-side technology or financial services transactions involving regulated financial institutions, digital assets, stablecoins, payments, cross-border transactions, or other fintech businesses.
  • Experience building, implementing, or scaling AI-enabled workflows, prompts, templates, playbooks, or tools for a legal team.

Who We Are:

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value:

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

  • Seek Excellence.
  • Be Selective To Be Effective.
  • Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
  • Disagree Transparently.
  • Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
  • Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are

You are a hands-on construction leader who has delivered large-scale, mission-critical data center or comparable infrastructure from start of construction through commissioning and turnover. You know what it takes to run a major building on a live campus: sequencing trades, protecting the schedule, and keeping safety and quality from becoming trade-offs. You lead teams from the front, hold contractors and partners to a high standard, and raise issues early and honestly. You are equally comfortable walking the building with a superintendent and presenting schedule, cost, and risk to senior leadership. You believe the digital economy depends on infrastructure delivered right, and delivered on time.

What You'll Do

As Senior Manager, Data Center Construction at Galaxy's Helios campus in Afton, TX, you will be Galaxy's accountable leader for construction of a large-scale data center building on the campus. You will report to the VP, Campus Construction Manager and work alongside peer Senior Managers who each own a building or scope, with shared accountability for the safety, schedule, cost, and quality standards that keep the campus aligned. You will own your building from preconstruction handoff through commissioning and turnover to operations, and you will lead the on-site Galaxy team and contractor relationships that make it happen.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own Data Center Facility Delivery: Serve as the single point of accountability for construction of a large-scale data center facility, from GMP handoff through energization, Level 1-5 commissioning, integrated systems testing (IST), and turnover to operations. Drive the facility to its safety, schedule, cost, and quality commitments.
  • Manage Schedule and Progress: Own the building schedule and track progress against baseline. Identify critical-path threats early, and direct recovery and mitigation plans before they affect milestones. Provide clear schedule inputs to the campus master schedule.
  • Manage Project Risk and Contingency: Maintain a quantified risk register covering schedule, cost, supply chain, labor, weather, and trade-interface risks. Control owner contingency drawdown, run structured risk reviews with the GC and trade partners, and drive mitigation before exposure becomes impact.
  • Drive Safety Culture: Set and enforce Galaxy's safety standards at the building level. Partner with Galaxy EHS and contractor safety leadership to sustain a zero-incident environment, and hold the team accountable for leading indicators as well as outcomes.
  • Oversee Contractors and Trade Partners: Manage the day-to-day and executive-level relationship with the general contractor and key trade partners. Ensure alignment on milestones, quality, safety, staffing, and commercial performance, and escalate issues early.
  • Control Cost and Change: Oversee pay applications, change orders, forecasts, and budget tracking for your building under the GMP. Enforce disciplined change management and provide accurate cost reporting to campus and executive leadership.
  • Lead Integrated Project Controls and Forecasting: Own the facility's integrated cost, schedule, and cash flow forecast on a monthly cycle. Validate GC-reported progress against independent percent-complete and earned value analysis, report cost-to-complete and forecast variances, and give development and finance leadership a reliable view of capital deployment and funding requirements.
  • Administer the Commercial Framework: Administer the GMP agreement and related owner contracts, including notices, allowances, buyout and savings, delay and impact claims, backcharges, retainage, and lien waivers. Protect Galaxy's commercial position and resolve disputes at the lowest level possible, partnering with Legal as needed.
  • Manage OFCI Integration: Work closely with Pre-Construction and the OFCI procurement and logistics teams to ensure UPS, generators, chillers, switchgear, and other owner-furnished equipment arrive, are set, and are installed without impacting the construction schedule.
  • Drive Utility and Energization Readiness: Coordinate with the serving utility, interconnect and substation teams, and Galaxy's power development group to align permanent power availability, energization sequencing, and test windows with construction and commissioning milestones. Treat power delivery as a critical-path item and escalate early.
  • Lead Commissioning and Turnover: Partner with the on-site commissioning manager, 3rd party Cx agent, and operations teams to ensure systematic testing, closeout, and clean turnover of the building to operations.
  • Manage Customer Delivery Commitments: Serve as the construction lead for customer-facing delivery milestones, including ready-for-service dates. Ensure facility handoff meets contractual commitments and the customer's acceptance criteria.
  • Ensure Quality: Enforce Galaxy's QA/QC standards on your building. Escalate and resolve systemic quality issues with contractors and design partners.

Coinflow is the next-generation payment service provider revolutionizing global financial infrastructure with stablecoins, AI-driven fraud prevention, and instant settlement. In response to this growth, Coinflow announced a $25M Series A in October 2025—led by Pantera Capital, CMT Digital, Coinbase Ventures, Jump Crypto, and Reciprocal Ventures—accelerating our mission to power the world’s fastest-moving businesses with innovative, reliable global payments.

Coinflow is proudly headquartered in Chicago, IL. Learn more at coinflow.cash.

About the Role

As we scale, we're making our first dedicated chargeback & fraud hire, a hands-on practitioner who will build our fraud function from the ground up: fraud tooling, investigations workflow, alert triage, and bank-partner reporting.

This role reports to our Risk Manager within the broader Risk & Compliance organization, and requires 5–8 years of relevant experience.

This is a builder role, not a maintainer role. You'll be the fraud subject-matter expert inside Coinflow, working alongside our BSA/AML Officer, Underwriters and Data Science, and will be the primary point of contact for fraud-related RFIs from our sponsor bank partners.

What You'll Do

Build the fraud function

  • Further develop and mature our existing transaction monitoring tool and investigations workflow, including case management, alerting logic, and evidence documentation standards.

  • Define SOPs, escalation paths, and decision frameworks for fraud investigations as the team's first dedicated hire.

Work alerts, investigations, and remediation

  • Monitor and triage fraud alerts across merchant and user/cardholder populations, investigating transaction patterns, account activity, and behavioral signals.

  • Conduct deep-dive investigations into suspected fraudulent merchants, card testing, account takeover, ACH fraud, and related fraud typologies.

  • Drive remediation: case disposition, funding actions, merchant/user offboarding recommendations, and root-cause analysis on confirmed fraud losses.

Identify and manage fraud risk vectors

  • Continuously assess Coinflow's exposure across merchant fraud (fraudulent merchant onboarding, bust-out schemes, transaction laundering) and user fraud (ATO, card testing, CNP fraud, ACH fraud, scams).

  • Track chargeback and fraud trends specific to our high-risk verticals (crypto on/off-ramps, gaming, remittance, digital goods) and recommend controls.

  • Monitor card network programs (VAMP, ECM/HECM, EFM, VIRP, BRAM, and new programs as they launch), in addition to NACHA program requirements, manage merchant remediation to stay below thresholds, and build workflows to meet new program requirements.

  • Track industry developments, network rule changes, and regulatory updates, and translate them into product and control recommendations.

Bank partner & stakeholder engagement

  • Serve as the primary owner of fraud-related RFIs from sponsor bank partners, preparing data, narratives, and supporting documentation.

  • Partner with the BSA/AML Officer and Data Science to align fraud and AML signal-sharing and investigations.

  • Present fraud metrics, trends, and program updates to Risk & Compliance leadership.

Operational Leadership (as the team grows)

  • Hire, train, and mentor fraud analysts.

  • Build out queue SLAs, escalation paths, and QA/calibration of analyst decisions.

  • Own the fraud playbooks and procedures.

Requirements

  • 5–8 years of experience in chargeback & fraud prevention, detection, investigations, or remediation within a payment service provider, Acquirer, or fintech platform.

  • Strong, hands-on understanding of fraud in the card acquiring space, covering both:

  • Merchant fraud: Fraudulent merchant onboarding/boarding fraud, transaction laundering, bust-out schemes, collusive merchant activity.

  • User/cardholder fraud: Account takeover (ATO), card testing, card-not-present (CNP) fraud, scams and social engineering.

  • Working knowledge of card brand fraud and chargeback monitoring programs such as VAMP, ECM, SMMP, VIRP, BRAM, etc., and experience remediating merchants against these thresholds.

  • Experience building or significantly improving fraud tooling, case management workflows, or investigations processes. This is a builder, not just an operator.

  • Comfortable responding directly to bank partner and sponsor bank RFIs, including preparing data and written narratives.

  • Highly analytical; comfortable using data to identify emerging fraud trends and to justify policy or tooling changes.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Able to explain complex fraud findings clearly to non-fraud stakeholders and external partners.

  • Sound judgment and ability to make and stand behind difficult, sometimes ambiguous, fraud decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with high-risk or emerging verticals such as crypto on/off-ramps, gaming, sweepstakes, digital goods.

  • SQL proficiency or comparable data skills to build dashboards, track fraud metrics, and drive investigations independently.

  • Familiarity with AML/KYC/underwriting processes and how fraud and onboarding signals intersect in a payments risk organization.

  • People leadership experience or a demonstrated path toward building and leading a fraud team over time.

  • Comfortable discussing complex merchant processing situations with Acquirers, Sponsor Banks, and the Card Networks.

descriptions.job-1jk86li:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

TRM is hiring a Strategic Finance Lead, R&D and AI to help decide how the company invests in AI, cloud and compute infrastructure, and the engineering capacity behind its products. You'll be the dedicated finance partner to the CTO and R&D leadership, turning complex usage, billing, and headcount data into recommendations that shape major investment decisions before they're made. Reporting to Pharoah Green, Head of Strategic Finance and FP&A, within the FP&A and Strategic Finance Business Partnership function, you'll design the financial architecture for R&D from the ground up, with AI built into how the work gets done.

The impact you will have:

  • Shape how TRM invests in AI, cloud, and compute by building an AI-assisted, driver-based economic model that connects usage and billing data across hundreds of SKUs to forecasts and decisions.

  • Lower R&D costs as a % of revenue without slowing product velocity, using AI to surface optimization opportunities in infrastructure spend and partnering with Engineering to act on them.

  • Define TRM's AI spend strategy with the Head of AI, using AI-powered analysis to track spend against ROI by tool and workload and to recommend where to commit, consolidate, or build.

  • Give R&D leaders an early view of change by owning planning, forecasting, and the headcount capacity model, with automated workflows that flag risks while there is still time to act.

  • Influence major infrastructure and R&D commitments by leading investment cases from business case to decision to measurement, with AI-assisted scenario analysis that makes tradeoffs clear.

  • Turn R&D performance into a clear executive and board narrative: what changed, why, and which decisions should follow.

  • Rebuild R&D finance around AI, automation, and Pigment so more time goes to shaping decisions and less to assembling reports.

What we're looking for:

  • 7+ years across strategic finance, FP&A, business operations, or a related role. We care more about the complexity you've owned and the influence you've had than an exact number of years.

  • A record of owning consequential work end to end: framing an ambiguous question, structuring the analysis, forming a point of view, and driving a recommendation to action.

  • Strong data-informed modeling skills, including driver-based forecasts, investment cases, and capacity models built from incomplete or complex data, accelerated with AI.

  • Hands-on experience analyzing cloud, compute, AI, or other usage-based technology costs, and experience partnering with Engineering, Product, Data, AI, or Infrastructure leaders.

  • The judgment and communication skills to become a trusted partner to senior technical leaders, challenge assumptions constructively, and explain financial implications in plain language.

  • Applied AI fluency: you can show how you've used AI to improve the speed or quality of modeling, research, or recurring workflows, and how you check the reliability of its output.

  • Curiosity to learn technical systems quickly and translate how AI products and modern infrastructure scale into financial insight.

About the Team:

  • Strategic Finance is a small, high-leverage team that works directly with TRM's leadership on planning, investment decisions, and company-wide strategy.

  • Our job isn't just to explain the numbers. We collaborate with leaders to make better decisions, and we hold a high bar for rigor and trust in our work.

  • You'll have substantial ownership from day one, direct exposure to the CTO and executive team, and room to shape how R&D finance operates.

  • The role is built to scale with its owner. Using AI and automation, you can expand what one person owns, and as the mandate grows there may be an opportunity to build a team.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • We're distributed, not distant: written communication for clarity and context, live time for decisions and collaboration.

  • Regular working sessions with the CTO and R&D leaders, plus a monthly R&D cost and forecast review.

  • Quarterly planning with Talent and R&D on headcount capacity, and annual planning cycles in Pigment.

  • Slack and Notion for async updates; AI tools are part of the daily workflow.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • Within your first 30 days, deliver an initial AI-assisted cloud forecast, focused on GCP with AWS coverage as applicable, that gives R&D leaders their first driver-based view of where infrastructure spend is heading.

  • Within your first 60 days, put a defined AI spend strategy in front of the CTO, with a clear recommendation on where to commit, consolidate, or cut.

  • Within your first 90 days, have the R&D capacity model integrated into the planning process so hiring decisions and budget move together.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.
